subject: Order of Independent Variables in procD.pgls

messages.author: 2725bf9dffb6e75f
messages.subject: Order of Independent Variables in procD.pgls
parts:
Hello,

I am using the procD.pgls function to test for an association between procrustes aligned skull landmark data of snake skulls of various species and several ecological variables. My independent variables include habitat use (categorical), and proportions of prey types consumed i.e. (propAmbibians, propAnnelids, propFishes, etc.). I am successfully running the PGLS analyses, however, I noticed that the order of the independent variables in the formula affects the p-values.

For example:

procD.pgls(shape ~ Habitat_Use+propAmphibians+propAnnelids, phy=phy, data=Figueroa_notroph)

obtains different p-value estimates for each variable than:

procD.pgls(shape ~ propAnnelids+Habitat_Use+propAmphibians, phy=phy, data=Figueroa_notroph)

I am not changing seed value or permutations (left at default). I had thought that order of main effects did not matter in a PGLS analysis, is there any reason why I may be getting these results with procD.pgls?

Thanks in advance,
Greg

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Order of Independent Variables in procD.pgls
parts:
Greg,

The default SS.type for that function is type I, sequential SS, in which case order does matter.  You could change this argument, i.e.,

SS.type = “III”

if you prefer type III, marginal SS, in which case the SS will not change based on order but the effect SS will also sum to more than the total SS.

Cheers!
Mike
